artifacts.summary: All 10 phases completed: relocated and rewrote setup/verify-lean-mcp.sh for per-project scope, added a SessionStart hook + installer for automatic zero-manual-step registration, inverted the verifier's drift semantics, extended the fixture suite, revised mcp-server-ownership.md and related docs, re-registered every active Lean project, and demonstrated concurrent-session acceptance across two project pairs.

completion_data.completion_summary: Replaced the single-global lean-lsp MCP registration with per-project entries under ~/.claude.json's .projects[<path>].mcpServers, written automatically at session start by a new SessionStart hook, inverting every artifact (verifier, preflight wrapper, fixture suite, recorded invariants) that previously enforced the single-global model. Demonstrated acceptance with two concurrent-session pairs, including a direct reproduction of the originally reported cross-project-answer defect, now resolved.

memory_candidates.content: On this machine, a Claude Code session's MCP tool registry is snapshotted independently of SessionStart hook execution: a hook that WRITES a new per-project ~/.claude.json registration during its own session's startup is NOT reliably visible within that same session, even though the write itself succeeds and is confirmed on disk. Measured directly: three sequential fresh `claude -p` sessions in a newly-registered directory -- the first (whose own hook invocation performed the write) still resolved a tool call against the stale/global config; only a later session saw the just-written entry. Any hook that writes to ~/.claude.json's registration (mcpServers, at either the top-level user scope or a .projects[<path>] local scope) should therefore always emit a same-session-may-be-stale notice (e.g. via additionalContext) rather than assume the write takes effect immediately.

A Claude Code hook that must fire in EVERY session on a machine, including inside a freshly created git worktree with no repository .claude/ deploy at all, cannot be contributed through an extension's settings-fragment.json (that only merges into a repo's OWN .claude/settings.local.json, which a deploy-less worktree never has). It must be installed at USER level instead: copy the hook script to a stable path under $HOME/.claude/hooks/, and merge the harness hook registration directly into $HOME/.claude/settings.json. If that file is also home-manager-managed and periodically reset from a dotfiles source (check the activation block's enforced-key list), the same registration must ALSO be written into that dotfiles source, or the next rebuild silently reverts it -- verify durability by re-running the activation's own enforced-key jq merge expression against the edited source before trusting the change.

~/.claude.json's per-project local scope (.projects["<abs path>"].mcpServers) takes precedence over the top-level global .mcpServers for that same project directory -- confirmed empirically (a project-scoped entry pointing at a DIFFERENT project than the global entry is the one that actually answers tool calls, from both a main session and a dispatched subagent). This makes local scope the correct registration surface for any MCP server needing per-project computed arguments where multiple such projects run concurrently on one machine -- a single global slot cannot hold more than one project's value at a time, and a stale global entry answers CONFIDENTLY WRONG rather than failing loudly, which is the most dangerous failure shape (it looks like success).
